mu_name_from: MuMain's ZzzOpenData.cpp loads the group as MODEL_MACE + i from Mace{i+1}, so Mace02.bmd is index 1, which OpenMU's 0.75 table names the Morning Star. MuWeapons.cs agrees from the client's side: `new("Morning Star", "Mace02.bmd", WeaponStance.Sword, ...)`.
why_this_one: Hanzo's counter is the last shop in Lorencia with lines that do not resolve, and this is one of them. A shelf drops what it cannot draw - shared/Market builds the row and leaves out anything whose group and number find no asset - so the blacksmith sold ten of his twenty-four lines and the rest of the counter was empty air. The first thing in group 2 the project has built, and it is two of Hanzo's lines rather than one: his slot 50 is written Scepters 1 at +2 and his slot 54 is written Scepters 1 at +3, so the Mace and the Morning Star on his shelf are the same row twice. That looks like a slip in OpenMU's store - the Morning Star is scepter index 1 and the Mace is index 0 - and shared/Market transcribes it as written rather than correcting a shelf nobody could then check. Building this row lights both cells.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Weapons.cs. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: CreateWeapon(group, number, slot, skillNumber, width, height, dropsFromMonsters, name, dropLevel, minimumDamage, maximumDamage, attackSpeed, durability, magicPower, levelRequirement, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, energyRequirement, vitalityRequirement, wizardClass, knightClass, elfClass).
stats.width_note: Width is where OpenMU keeps two-handedness - `if (group < Bows && width == 2)` - and one here agrees with MuWeapons.cs's TwoHanded: false. It is also what takes a fifth off the price: shared/Market.Coin reads the footprint's width to tell a one-handed weapon from a two-handed one.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are the wizard, knight and elf flags, and MuWeapons.cs carries the same set from the client's side.
stats.skill_note: The skillNumber of the call. There are no skills in this simulation, so it is carried for the row to read against the call it came from and nothing more - and it is the reason this item is dearer in the original than the price MU2 charges, since OpenMU multiplies a skilled item's price by two and a half. See shared/Market's remarks.

stance_from: MuWeapons.cs: WeaponStance.Sword, TwoHanded: false. Actions 4 and 17, the family the Kris, the Short Sword and the Hand Axe already walk in. A one-handed blade leaves the shield hand free, which is the whole point of it on a counter that is mostly shields.
sheet_from: Data/Item/mace03.OZJ (16x16), from MuMain. The .bmd names mace03.jpg; 118 triangles, one mesh - the most triangles of anything in this batch, on the smallest sheet in the project. Sixteen square is the whole of what MU shipped for it, and after the 3x that is 48 square; no amount of anything gets more out of it.
material_note:
Sixteen pixels square, which is the smallest sheet in the project, and a hundred and eighteen triangles standing on it. There is very little to read and the reading is honest about that: three bands and a column, and the islands take one each.

Island 2 is the head - ninety-eight of the triangles, the spiked ball above Z 70 - at (65, 64, 57) and chroma 14. Achromatic, and a struck head rather than a ground edge, so plate_steel: cast pitting with no direction in it, which is what survives being laid out over a ball of spikes.

Island 0 is the shaft at (132, 118, 105) chroma 26, the pale band along the top of the sheet. steel, and here the brushed grain is right - it is a drawn rod and the grain runs along it.

Island 1 is the grip at (145, 104, 81) chroma 64, the brown column up the right of the sheet with pale studs in it. leather_wrap.

The grip was leather_wrap and it striped, which is what leather.json exists to stop: its grain is the winding, a weave along u at scale 90 and depth 0.55, and on a broad face that is corduroy rather than a cord. leather keeps the substance and swaps the winding for isotropic pebbling. Same fault, same day, as the arrow quiver's bag.

Island 1 went leather_wrap to leather to wood over two passes. leather_wrap striped it, which is that material's weave on a broad face. leather stopped the striping and was still the wrong substance: the island is (145, 104, 81) at chroma 64, a brown rod with pale studs set into it, and a rod is turned timber rather than hide. wood's grain runs along the length at depth 0.08, an eighth of leather_wrap's, so it says the thing is wooden without banding it.
open_question: Sixteen square is 48 after the 3x and no amount of anything gets more out of it. The materials are doing more of the work on this item than on anything else here, because the albedo cannot: what it carries is four colours and a gradient.
